events.title: Publication of Uncle Tom's Cabin
events.description: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel Uncle Tom's Cabin was published in book form in Boston by John P. Jewett, after being serialized in the abolitionist newspaper The National Era.
events.significance: The novel became one of the best-selling books of the 19th century and greatly intensified anti-slavery sentiment in the Northern United States, helping to shape public opinion in the lead-up to the American Civil War.

events.title: Einstein Publishes the Theory of General Relativity
events.description: Albert Einstein's paper 'The Foundation of the General Theory of Relativity' appeared in the journal Annalen der Physik, presenting a complete formulation of general relativity.
events.significance: General relativity redefined gravity as the curvature of spacetime and became a cornerstone of modern physics, underpinning our understanding of black holes, gravitational waves, and cosmology.

events.title: Tunisia Gains Independence from France
events.description: France formally recognized Tunisia's independence by signing a protocol, ending the French protectorate established in 1881. Habib Bourguiba became the leader of the new state.
events.significance: Tunisia's independence was a key moment in the decolonization of North Africa and set the stage for the country's development as a modern republic under Bourguiba.

events.title: Tokyo Subway Sarin Gas Attack
events.description: Members of the doomsday cult Aum Shinrikyo released sarin nerve gas on several Tokyo subway lines during morning rush hour, killing 13 people and injuring thousands more.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest terrorist attacks in Japanese history and a landmark case of chemical terrorism, prompting major changes in Japan's counterterrorism and emergency response policies worldwide.

events.title: Invasion of Iraq Begins
events.description: A US-led coalition launched military operations against Iraq, beginning with airstrikes on Baghdad and a ground invasion from Kuwait, on the grounds of alleged weapons of mass destruction and Saddam Hussein's regime.
events.significance: The invasion toppled Saddam Hussein's government and began a prolonged conflict that reshaped the politics of the Middle East and sparked global debate over the legitimacy and consequences of the war.
